beats.caption: Good evening. We interrupt your scrolling with a story so big it needed its own feed.

data.headline: Local engineer builds entire portfolio by talking at his laptop
data.ticker: Keyboard reportedly feeling left out  •  Wispr Flow confirms involvement  •  Emergent credits described as nervous  •  More at eleven

beats.caption: Sources confirm he spoke every idea out loud. No typing. Not even a semicolon.
It's genuinely faster. I think in sentences, not in keystrokes.
Thinking in SENTENCES, folks. Experts are calling it: talking.
Back to you, Reginald. Reginald? He's asleep. Classic Reginald.

comments.text: I was not asleep. I was observing. Quietly.
A man talks to a computer. In my day we called that a phone call.
the ticker is giving ✨production value✨

beats.caption: Here, in the corridors of a Pune university, we find a rare creature.
The young engineer has found something missing. A place for builders to gather.
So he does what few of his kind attempt. He builds the community himself, from nothing.
Two hundred members. Hackathons of a hundred. Sponsors. Remarkable.
And the creature's reward? A title. GitHub Campus Expert. The only one his university has ever had.

comments.text: TWO HUNDRED MEMBERS?? That's a stadium, Reggie!
It is not a stadium, Blaze. It is a WhatsApp group.
Did anyone bring snacks to these gatherings. Asking for myself.

beats.caption: Ladies and gentlemen, let's go to the numbers.
Six hundred days. Every. Single. Day. Spanish.
Hola. That's most of what I can say with confidence.
That's commitment, folks. That's a man the owl fears.

comments.text: obsessed with consistency as a personality trait
Six hundred days and he still can't order a coffee. Impressive, in a way.
Persistence. The most underrated survival trait.

beats.caption: Leaving a review for Saurav.
Builds things nobody asked for. Then everybody ends up using them.
Very polite. Answers emails. Suspiciously organised.
Made a whole website about himself starring cartoon animals. Including me. Unpaid.
Three and a half stars. Half a star off for the unpaid part.

comments.text: THREE AND A HALF is Marge's HIGHEST SCORE EVER
It is not. I gave a radiator four once.
I'll take it.

beats.caption: Today's myth. One I hear far too often.

data.myth: You need a referral to land your first internship.
data.fact: Saurav cold-emailed his way into his first one. The audacity.

beats.caption: No connections. No referral. Just a polite, specific email to the right person.
Write to people. Most of them answer. Some of them even hire you.

comments.text: cold emailing is literally just sliding into DMs for LinkedIn people
Bold behaviour for a young engineer. I approve.

beats.caption: Okay so listen. Saurav's family runs a manufacturing business.
And they need new buyers. Like, actual factories that buy metal parts.
So instead of cold calling, he builds a whole automated outreach pipeline. Himself. On weekends.
The tools say every email address is verified. Perfect, right? Right??

comments.text: I'm on the edge of my seat and I'm not even sitting
Verified by whom. That's what I'd like to know.

beats.caption: Okay so. He doesn't just trust the tool. He actually checks.
Two of the five "verified" addresses he could test were just... wrong.
So now every campaign gets checked by hand before anything goes out. The tool is a suggestion, not a fact.
Lesson of the day: trust, but verify the verified. Iconic.

comments.text: Told you. Verified by whom.
A healthy scepticism. Rare, and valuable.
part 3 when he finds the buyers?? 👀

beats.caption: Welcome back to the show! Tonight's guest built a whole website starring cartoon animals.

data.topic: Why build a portfolio like this?

beats.caption: A normal portfolio gets skimmed in ten seconds. I wanted people to actually stay.
Ten seconds?! Folks, that's shorter than my intro!
Exactly. So I made it something you scroll.
Saurav, everybody! Stay for the cartoon animals!

comments.text: I was not consulted about being a cartoon animal.
the host is giving late-night energy fr
Retention, by way of tortoise. Bold.

beats.caption: I've been asked to rank Saurav's tools. Against my will.
Java. Old, reliable, never surprises anyone. Like me. S.
React. Changes its mind every year. B.
TypeScript. Tells you you're wrong before you are. A.
AI engineering. Ask me again in a year. C, for now.

comments.text: JAVA IN S TIER?? Marge has SPOKEN
react in B tier?? i'm shaking
Fair, honestly.

This man calls talking to a laptop news.
In my day we talked to people. They didn't listen either.
Still. The website is nice. Don't tell him I said that.

comments.text: MARGE STITCHED ME. I'M FRAMING THIS
stitch of the year honestly

beats.caption: Day one. He's already asked where the docs are.
Day three. The docs exist now. He wrote them.
Week two. The thing nobody owned? He owns it now.
Month one. You're wondering why you didn't hire him sooner.
